en: The Banaue Rice Terraces act as a giant inclined plane, reducing the force needed for Ifugao farmers to carry crops up steep mountains.
Wearing rubber tsinelas on wet, polished bamboo floors is dangerous because the smooth surface provides very little friction to stop slipping.
A falling coconut from a tree in Davao accelerates toward the ground at 9.8 meters per second squared due to Earth's gravity.
The black sand beaches of Camarines Norte contain magnetite, a naturally magnetic iron ore that can be attracted to a compass needle.
The Makiling-Banahaw geothermal power plant in Laguna converts thermal energy from underground hot water into the electricity that powers nearby homes.
Fireflies, locally called aninipot, produce their own cold light in Dapitan City through a chemical reaction inside their abdomens called bioluminescence.
Shouting inside the Puerto Princesa Underground River creates an echo because sound waves bounce back from the hard limestone cave walls.
A traditional clay palayok acts as a thermal insulator, distributing heat slowly and evenly to cook sticky rice kakanin without burning it.
The woven sails of an Iloilo paraw sailboat capture wind energy, transforming it into the kinetic energy needed to move across water.
Eating a sweet banana cue during recess gives a Grade 5 student chemical energy stored in the saba banana's carbohydrates.
A farmer in Bukidnon uses a sharp steel bolo as a wedge to split open hard coconuts with less applied force.
The smooth, waxy surface of a gabi leaf reduces fluid friction, allowing rainwater to easily roll off without soaking the plant.
